title: March-to-November flow ratios fell, but flexible autumn adjustment left uncertain winter trends at three Arctic gauges in 1981-2011
abstract: We tested winter flow change at Ob-Salekhard, Lena-Kyusyur and Yenisey-Igarka with ArcticGRO v20261104. In 30 common certified winter years from 1981 to 2011, the equal-river mean trend in March flow divided by prior November flow was -9.72% per decade. The conditional 95% three-year block limits were -13.38% to -5.97%. March flow rose in each fitted record, but November flow rose faster. A planned model that estimated the autumn flow coefficient gave a mean time trend of -2.14% per decade, with limits of -6.13% to +1.99%. Thus, the falling ratio alone does not establish faster winter depletion. Five-year blocks, February-March flow and an October denominator retained negative mean ratio trends. The flexible model did not resolve a remaining time trend. This is a historical gauge association, not a test of groundwater, reservoirs, ice effects or ocean salinity. Few rivers, short records, revised data, model assumptions and conditional uncertainty limit the result. Code, source hashes, aggregate evidence, a figure and an arithmetic audit support reproduction. External source records remain outside the package.

display.caption: Seasonal flow ratios and equal-river trend estimates. Bars show conditional 95% residual block limits. The flexible model estimates the autumn coefficient instead of fixing it at one.
